children: Etihad Airways is set to unveil a new generation of its global lounge experience, beginning with a transformed lounge at London Heathrow in summer 2027 as part of a wider expansion of its premium ground offering.

The Heathrow lounge will be the first to fully introduce the airline’s new Beyond Borders design language, establishing a new design approach intended to create stronger visual and experiential connections between Etihad’s lounges and aircraft.
The initiative forms part of the airline’s wider Beyond Borders product and experience strategy, which aims to deliver greater consistency across the customer journey.

Etihad is investing in aircraft, lounges, dining, amenities, wellbeing, connectivity and service as part of a reported $20 billion investment in new aircraft and customer experience, including a $1 billion fleet retrofit programme.
The transformed London Heathrow Lounge will provide the first complete expression of the new lounge concept.
Visitors to Etihad’s ATM stand were given an early preview of elements planned for the new facility, including a central showpiece feature and a new bar design.
The design concept will subsequently be extended to new Etihad lounges across the airline’s network.
The lounges will serve as premium gateways to the Etihad experience, reflecting the design language and hospitality principles being introduced across the airline’s Beyond Borders products.
Each lounge will include dedicated areas for Business and First guests, as well as private suites for passengers travelling in The Residence.

Arik De, Chief Revenue and Commercial Officer at Etihad Airways, said: “Our new lounges are an important part of the Etihad experience and London Heathrow marks the beginning of an exciting new chapter. It will be the first lounge to bring our new design language fully to life on the ground, creating a space that feels uniquely Etihad and distinctly connected to Abu Dhabi.

“The thinking behind Beyond Borders is that our guests should increasingly recognise the same Etihad identity wherever they are in their journey. That doesn't mean every space or every aircraft needs to be identical, but there should be a clear connection through our design, hospitality, dining, wellbeing and service.

“London is the beginning. As we expand our lounge network, we have an opportunity to create a more consistent premium experience on the ground while continuing to bring the warmth and character of Abu Dhabi to our guests around the world.”

The new design language is rooted in Abu Dhabi and draws on the concept of “sand to superstructure”, reflecting the emirate’s natural landscape, architecture and development. The approach was first introduced through Etihad’s new aircraft interiors and will now extend into lounges through shared materials, textures, lighting and distinctive design elements.
Rather than replicating identical spaces, the concept will establish recognisable design touchpoints while allowing individual lounges to reflect their location and purpose.
The announcement follows the world debut of Etihad’s new A330 cabin at ATM, alongside the presentation of the Beyond Borders design on its A321LR.
Together, the aircraft and lounge developments represent the next stage of the airline’s effort to create a connected experience across airports, lounges, aircraft and destinations.
London Heathrow will mark the start of the new global lounge programme, with further developments planned as Etihad continues to expand its network and extend the Beyond Borders experience.
